findings.problem: Two proofs (lines 25–35 and 126–137) repeat the same 10-line `Finset.sum_bij` argument showing that a sum is unchanged when you precompose with an involution; one uses `cubeFlip`, the other `cubeToggle i`. Building on these, `coefficient_zero_of_odd` (lines 40–43) and `conditioned_coefficient_zero_invalid` (lines 158–161) repeat the same follow-up step. Each one rewrites the involuted sum with a sign-reversal identity, applies `Finset.sum_neg_distrib`, and finishes with `linarith` to conclude S = -S, hence S = 0. Only the involution and the anti-invariance fact change between the two copies.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one shared lemma (the variable context `[Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]` already holds):
```lean
theorem sum_eq_zero_of_involutive_neg {σ : Cube I → Cube I}
    (hσ : Function.Involutive σ) (F : Cube I → ℝ)
    (hF : ∀ f, F (σ f) = -F f) : ∑ f, F f = 0 := by
  have h := hσ.bijective.sum_comp F   -- ∑ F (σ f) = ∑ F f
  simp_rw [hF, Finset.sum_neg_distrib] at h
  linarith
```
If the involution-invariance lemmas are still wanted, they become one-liners:
- `sum_cubeFlip F := (Function.Involutive.bijective (f := cubeFlip) cubeFlip_cubeFlip).sum_comp F`
- `sum_cubeToggle i F := (Function.Involutive.bijective (cubeToggle_twice i)).sum_comp F`

The two zero-coefficient proofs then become:
```lean
theorem coefficient_zero_of_odd (F) (hF : ∀ f, F (cubeFlip f) = -F f) : ... := by
  have hs := sum_eq_zero_of_involutive_neg cubeFlip_cubeFlip F hF
  simp [coefficient, walsh, bitSign, Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card, hs]

theorem conditioned_coefficient_zero_invalid ... (hi : valid i = false) (hs : s i = true) : ... := by
  have hz := sum_eq_zero_of_involutive_neg (cubeToggle_twice i)
    (fun f => B (restrictQuery valid f) * walsh s f)
    (fun f => by rw [restrictQuery_cubeToggle valid i hi, walsh_cubeToggle s i f hs, mul_neg])
  simp [coefficient, Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card, hz]
```
findings.benefit: The Fourier cancellation principle (an odd function under a fixed-point-free symmetry averages to zero) is stated once. Each proof then reads as "this is anti-invariant under this involution", instead of re-deriving a bijection and a `linarith` step. It also drops two hand-written `sum_bij` proofs in favour of existing Mathlib API, and a future third symmetry (for example, toggling a set of coordinates) only needs its anti-invariance fact.

findings.proposed_change:
Keep the counting argument only in `majorityBit_count`. Move `majority_exists` below it and derive it from it:
```lean
theorem majority_exists (g : Index → Bool) :
    ∃ b : Bool, 24 ≤ indices.countP (fun i => g i == b) :=
  ⟨majorityBit g, majorityBit_count g⟩
```
Since the existential is unused, deleting it is also an option.
findings.benefit: The pigeonhole step (one of the two values occurs at least 24 times among 48 indices) is proved once, by the version with the explicit witness. If `indices` or the threshold 24 changes, only one proof needs updating. Readers also see directly that the existential follows from the computable `majorityBit`.
